simple.meaning: חֲמוֹת (chămôwth) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a mother-in-law.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across Ruth, Micah, beginning at Ruth 1:14. Its contexts include family, family line, Torah, city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲמוֹת (H2545).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֲמוֹת (chămôwth) / H2545 is traced through Ruth 1:14, Ruth 2:11, Ruth 2:18, Ruth 2:19 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: They lifted up their voices and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth stayed with her.

Boaz answered her, “I have been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you have left your father, your mother, and the land of your birth, and have come to a people that you didn’t know before.
She took it up, and went into the city. Then her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave to her that which she had left after she had enough.
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you.”
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you.”
So she stayed close to the maidens of Boaz, to glean to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
She went down to the threshing floor, and did everything that her mother-in-law told her.
When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “How did it go, my daughter?”
She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley; for he said, ‘Don’t go empty to your mother-in-law.’ ”
For the son dishonors the father,

definitions.full: H2545. chamoth [ חָמוֺת ] noun feminine husband's mother (Late Hebrew חָמוֺת , Aramaic חֲמָתָא ; Arabic husband's mother ; Assyrian êmêtu , Zim BP 48 ; Ethiopic ) — only suffix חֲמוֺתֵךְ Ruth 2:11 ; 3:17 ; חֲמוֺתָהּ 1:14 7 t.; חֲמֹתָהּ Micah 7:6 ; — of Naomi Ruth 1:14 ; 2:11 , 18 , 19 (twice in verse); 2:23 ; 3:1 , 6 , 16 , 17 ; בַּחֲמֹתָהּ כַּלָּה בְאִמָּ֔הּ קָמָ֫ה בַּת Micah 7:6 .
